panels.title: Head height
panels.description: Canonical head block number, set by forkchoiceUpdated. A flat line means the node stopped following the chain.

panels.title: Peers
panels.description: Connected devp2p peers. Few peers means a thin mempool and a slow block import.

panels.title: Block building time
panels.description: Time the last payload took to build. This is the builder's core latency.

panels.title: Build throughput
panels.description: Ggas/s reached while building the last payload.

panels.title: Execution time
panels.description: Time to execute the last imported block.

panels.title: engine p99 latency
panels.description: 99th percentile Engine API handling time. The consensus client blocks on this.

panels.title: RPC error ratio
panels.description: Share of RPC and Engine API calls that returned an error.

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: Process RSS.

panels.title: Head height and block number
panels.description: Chain head against the last block the node executed. A widening gap means the node falls behind.

panels.title: Block building time
panels.description: Payload build time per instance. This value is a gauge that the node overwrites after each block, not a histogram. Read it as the last sample, and use the legend minimum, mean, and maximum for the spread.

panels.title: Engine API and RPC — the consensus client's critical path
Engine API latency p99 by method
panels.description: 99th percentile handling time per Engine API method. engine_newPayload and engine_forkchoiceUpdated gate the whole building cycle.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, method) (rate(rpc_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", namespace="engine", method=~"$rpc_method"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Engine API latency p50 by method
panels.description: Median handling time per Engine API method.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, method) (rate(rpc_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", namespace="engine", method=~"$rpc_method"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Engine API call rate
panels.description: Engine API calls per second by method.

panels.title: Engine API errors
panels.description: Failed Engine API calls per second, split by error kind.

targets.expr: sum by (method, error_kind) (rate(rpc_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", namespace="engine", outcome="error", method=~"$rpc_method"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Engine API time share
panels.description: Wall-clock seconds per second spent inside each Engine API method. This shows the method that costs the most in total, not the one that is slowest per call.

panels.title: Engine API latency distribution
panels.description: Full Engine API latency histogram over time.

panels.title: eth RPC latency p99 by method
panels.description: Ten slowest public JSON-RPC methods at the 99th percentile.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, method) (rate(rpc_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", namespace="rpc", method=~"$rpc_method"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: eth RPC call rate and errors
panels.description: Public JSON-RPC calls per second by outcome.

panels.title: Build time and throughput
panels.description: Payload build time against the gas throughput it reached. This value is a gauge that the node overwrites after each block, not a histogram. Read it as the last sample, and use the legend minimum, mean, and maximum for the spread.

panels.title: Base fee of the built block
panels.description: Base fee per gas of the last built payload. This value is a gauge that the node overwrites after each block, not a histogram. Read it as the last sample, and use the legend minimum, mean, and maximum for the spread.

panels.title: Transactions included by type
panels.description: Transactions added to a payload per second, by transaction type. This is the builder's real inclusion rate.

panels.title: Transaction execution errors
panels.description: Transactions that failed during payload building, by error. A rise wastes build time and lowers block value.

panels.title: Transaction error ratio
panels.description: Share of attempted transactions that failed during building.

panels.title: Transactions in the last block
panels.description: Transaction count of the last processed block. This value is a gauge that the node overwrites after each block, not a histogram. Read it as the last sample, and use the legend minimum, mean, and maximum for the spread.

panels.title: Block processing stage times
panels.description: Time per stage for the last imported block. The tallest series is the import bottleneck. This value is a gauge that the node overwrites after each block, not a histogram. Read it as the last sample, and use the legend minimum, mean, and maximum for the spread.

panels.title: Total block import time
panels.description: Execution, merkle, store, and validate added together. Compare this with the slot budget.

targets.expr: execution_ms{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} + merkle_ms{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} + store_ms{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} + validate_ms{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Merkle concurrency
panels.description: Merkle work done next to execution against work left over after execution ends. A large drain time means the merkle pipeline does not overlap well.

panels.title: Merkle overlap
panels.description: Share of merkle work that ran concurrently with execution. A fall here directly raises import time.

panels.title: State warmer
panels.description: Warmer thread time, and whether the warmer finished before execution needed the state. A negative early value means the warmer is late and execution waits on cold state.

panels.title: Execution throughput
panels.description: Gas throughput of the last imported block. This value is a gauge that the node overwrites after each block, not a histogram. Read it as the last sample, and use the legend minimum, mean, and maximum for the spread.

panels.title: Execution throughput p50 and p10
panels.description: Distribution of execution throughput. The low quantile is the interesting one: it shows the worst blocks.

panels.title: Gas used and gas limit
panels.description: Gas consumed by the last processed block, and how full it was.

panels.title: Function profiling — where the node spends its time
Slowest functions p99
panels.description: Fifteen slowest instrumented functions at the 99th percentile. This is the fastest way to find a new bottleneck in block processing.

targets.expr: topk(15, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, namespace, function_name) (rate(function_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Function time share
panels.description: Wall-clock seconds per second inside each instrumented function. Unlike the p99 panel, this ranks by total cost, so a cheap function called often shows up here.

panels.title: Function call rate
panels.description: Calls per second for the most frequent instrumented functions.

panels.title: Function mean duration
panels.description: Mean duration of the most expensive instrumented functions.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (namespace, function_name) (rate(function_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (namespace, function_name) (rate(function_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: devp2p networking — mempool and block supply
Peer count
panels.description: Connected devp2p peers.

panels.title: Inbound msg rate
panels.description: devp2p messages received per second.

panels.title: Outbound msg rate
panels.description: devp2p messages sent per second.

panels.title: Disconnect rate
panels.description: Peer disconnections per second. A high rate means the peer set keeps churning and the mempool view stays thin.

panels.title: discv4 in rate
panels.description: discv4 discovery messages received per second.

panels.title: discv5 in rate
panels.description: discv5 discovery messages received per second.

panels.title: Peer count
panels.description: Connected peers over time.

panels.title: Peers by client
panels.description: Peer set split by client software. A set dominated by one client is a supply risk.

panels.title: devp2p message rate by type
panels.description: devp2p messages per second by type. Watch Transactions and NewPooledTransactionHashes: they feed the mempool the builder sells from.

panels.title: Disconnections by reason
panels.description: Peer disconnections per second by reason.

panels.title: Discovery message rate
panels.description: Discovery traffic per second.

panels.title: Kademlia operation latency
panels.description: Kademlia table operation time. A slow full scan blocks the discovery loop.

panels.title: Sync stage and peers
panels.description: Sync stage, the peers that can serve snap data, and the request pipeline depth. Few snap peers is the usual cause of a stalled sync.

panels.title: Pivot freshness
panels.description: Age of the snap-sync pivot block. When this grows past the state window the pivot must move and work is lost.

panels.title: Header download progress
panels.description: Headers fetched against headers required.

panels.title: State download progress
panels.description: Account and storage trie download and insert progress.

panels.title: Healing progress
panels.description: Trie leaves repaired during the heal phase.

panels.title: Bytecode download progress
panels.description: Contract bytecodes fetched against bytecodes required.

panels.title: Sync request outcomes
panels.description: Snap-sync request outcomes per second. A rising failure share means the peers cannot serve the data.

panels.title: Sync phase start time
panels.description: Unix timestamp at which each sync phase began. A value that stops advancing marks the phase the sync is stuck in.

panels.title: Reorg depth
panels.description: Depth of attempted reorgs and how often they happen. A deep reorg throws away built state.

panels.title: Reorg reconcile time
panels.description: Time to reconcile state on the first commit after a reorg. This blocks block production.

panels.title: Deep reorg outcomes
panels.description: Deep reorg attempts and how they ended. Aborts leave the node on a stale head.

panels.title: Reorg overlay size
panels.description: Size of the installed reorg overlay and the span of the state-history journal. Zero entries means no reorg is in progress.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: CPU cores consumed by the builder process.

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: Process RSS.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Open file descriptors.

panels.title: FD headroom
panels.description: File descriptors left before the process hits its limit.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: OS threads in the process.

panels.title: Datadir size
panels.description: Bytes on disk under the configured datadir.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: Cores consumed over time. A flat ceiling means the builder is CPU-bound.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Process memory. Steady RSS growth is a leak.

panels.title: File descriptors
panels.description: Open file descriptors against the process limit.

panels.title: Datadir size
panels.description: Disk consumed by the datadir. The metrics handler walks the directory on every scrape, so a large datadir makes scrapes slow.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: OS threads.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the process started. A reset marks a restart.
